requirement: Accept DOCX, UTF-8 TXT and Markdown resumes; reject unsupported formats.
acceptance: Each supported file reaches the parser. An unsupported extension returns HTTP 400. PDF support is specified in FR-1.8.

requirement: Reject empty, oversized or unreadable resumes and explain the cause.
acceptance: An empty file, a file above 5 MiB within the request limit, or an unparseable document returns HTTP 400. The outer request limit is separate.

requirement: Extract the stated name, title, contacts, summary, categorized skills, education, experience, projects, certifications and achievements.
acceptance: Recognized sections retain the candidate's wording; the parser splits headings and bullets into fields and leaves absent sections empty.

requirement: Extract work mode, preferred locations, minimum salary, work authorization and employment types only from explicit statements.
acceptance: A preference line or explicit summary statement supplies a value. An employer's location or a skill alone does not establish a preference.

requirement: Warn consistently about a missing name, email, skill list, summary or work history.
acceptance: Missing or invalid email and empty core fields produce named warnings. The work-history warning requires both experience and projects to be absent.

requirement: Persist the extracted profile and return an identifier for later retrieval.
acceptance: The owner can use the returned profile ID to retrieve the same structured data without uploading again.

requirement: Validate document contents and store each upload under a server-generated name.
acceptance: DOCX must open as a Word ZIP package; TXT and MD must decode as UTF-8. The client filename does not select the stored path.

requirement: Parse PDF resumes into candidate profiles.
acceptance: A readable text-layer PDF yields a profile. Encrypted, damaged, image-only or undecodable PDFs receive a reason; no OCR is provided.

requirement: Keep an uploaded resume in the caller's directory and prevent another account from retrieving it.
acceptance: Two ordinary accounts receive different storage roots; a foreign document ID cannot download the file.

requirement: Let the candidate confirm work eligibility for named countries separately from sponsorship and citizenship.
acceptance: Eligibility for one country does not establish eligibility elsewhere. Without a usable country or a relevant declaration, the answer remains unknown.

requirement: Keep voluntary equal-opportunity information separate from ordinary profile facts.
acceptance: Nonempty selections require opt-in, can be deleted, and are excluded from ranking and tailoring. Declining to answer is not selected automatically.

requirement: Retrieve listings only from the public Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby and Remotive APIs.
acceptance: The source registry contains those four adapters. Listing discovery does not scrape employer pages.

requirement: Construct discovery URLs from provider hosts and validated board or posting identifiers.
acceptance: An invalid Greenhouse token or Lever slug issues no request; a board name cannot replace the adapter's host.

requirement: Refuse non-HTTP(S) source URLs and destinations that resolve to nonpublic addresses before fetching them.
acceptance: A loopback, private, link-local or reserved result in the DNS answer causes refusal before the HTTP request.

requirement: Pace requests to each host and retry only transient source failures.
acceptance: The default interval is one second. Transport errors, 429 and 5xx permit two retries with backoff; redirects and other 4xx fail without retry.

requirement: Normalize each accepted posting to a JobListing with a canonical ID, title and company.
acceptance: A posting missing an identifier, title or company does not enter the corpus; source identity remains available on the stored row.

requirement: Extract skills from listing text with a fixed vocabulary.
acceptance: A recognized term or alias produces its canonical skill; the extractor does not add an unrelated skill from the job title or occupation alone.

requirement: Remove duplicate listings and insert or update each posting by its canonical ID.
acceptance: Refreshing the same source records twice updates existing rows without increasing the job count.

requirement: Embed only new or changed listing text and preserve completed work when a quota ends the run.
acceptance: Unchanged indexed text incurs no new embedding. An interrupted refresh reports partial progress and can continue with outstanding texts.

requirement: Continue a refresh when one source fails and identify that source in the report.
acceptance: A failing source has a named error; listings returned by other configured sources remain eligible for storage.

requirement: Keep the LinkedIn source adapter unregistered.
acceptance: Normal discovery cannot select LinkedIn and makes no LinkedIn request.

requirement: Screen likely machine-generated or repetitive listings before storing or embedding them.
acceptance: The deterministic screen drops entries that meet its spam rules and reports a count; the verdict does not establish who authored a posting.

requirement: Limit new listings per source, per refresh and across the corpus; report exclusions.
acceptance: The admission report counts listings denied by each applicable bound. Existing rows can still receive updates.

requirement: At capacity, evict eligible listings in order of their last sighting.
acceptance: Eviction is bounded. A referenced listing, one never seen, or one from a failed source is not removed to make room.

requirement: Budget embeddings by cache miss, share work across sources and stop at the daily limit.
acceptance: Cache hits consume no work allowance. With several sources waiting, the refresh allocates work across them and reports a partial run on exhaustion.

requirement: Neutralize board HTML in one bounded, forward scan.
acceptance: Long malformed markup does not trigger repeated scans of the remaining string. Retained text can be displayed without interpreting the source markup.

requirement: Queue a refresh durably and expose its progress independently of the initiating request.
acceptance: POST /api/jobs/refresh returns HTTP 202 and a run ID. Closing the browser does not cancel the worker's stored work items.

requirement: Merge equivalent postings returned by different sources without merging separate IDs from a single source on that basis.
acceptance: Matching normalized company, title and location can produce one surviving posting. Provider-specific change stamps do not transfer to another provider.

requirement: Search stored listings without contacting a job board.
acceptance: With adapters unavailable, search still ranks matching local records; an empty corpus returns an empty result set.

requirement: Score semantic similarity, skills, experience, seniority, location and preferences on a 0 to 100 scale with published default weights.
acceptance: The original weights (0.20, 0.30, 0.20, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10) are superseded. The current eight-component distribution is given in section 3.2.3.

requirement: Accept only a complete set of positive weight overrides totaling 1.0 within 0.01.
acceptance: Startup rejects incomplete, extra or nonpositive weights and totals outside tolerance. Overrides now require eight named components instead of six.

requirement: Distinguish missing inputs from hard conflicts when scoring a component.
acceptance: The proposed neutral 70 is not used: missing inputs contribute zero with an unknown state. Explicit conflicts such as incompatible work mode can score 25.

requirement: Derive semantic scores from cosine similarity between the candidate's query vector and listing vectors.
acceptance: For a nondegenerate vector pair, cosine similarity times 100 is clamped to 0 to 100; a measured zero is distinguishable from a missing vector.

requirement: Return a degraded ranking when embeddings are unavailable.
acceptance: The original fallback redistributed the semantic weight. The current blend keeps it in the denominator, contributes zero for the missing vector and reports reduced coverage.

requirement: Explain each returned result with component scores, matched skills and missing skills.
acceptance: The result includes component states, a readable explanation and evidence coverage, even when no semantic score is available.

requirement: Filter stored jobs by query terms and a case-insensitive location substring.
acceptance: Any query token of at least two characters in the title or description satisfies the text filter. The location filter applies independently.

requirement: Return the highest overall scores in descending order and store a match per returned result.
acceptance: A top-N search returns up to N results in score order and links the corresponding match rows to the requesting profile.

requirement: Retrieve a listing by ID and return the profile's matches in chronological order.
acceptance: The default history is newest first, not the original oldest-first order. Ranked mode selects the latest match per job and sorts by score.

requirement: Do not let missing skill requirements confer a ranking advantage over a genuine partial skill match.
acceptance: With other components held equal, no stated skills earns zero skill credit; a positive partial match earns credit. Other evidence may still change the overall order.

requirement: Measure lexical overlap and occupational fit as separate sources of ranking evidence.
acceptance: BM25 scores posting text; role relevance compares the posting's job family with candidate targets. A classified hard role mismatch caps the overall score at 25.

requirement: Extract job requirements from structured fields and skill mentions without calling a language model.
acceptance: Preserve stated requirements and identify candidate skills actually mentioned in the description. Missing fields do not generate new requirements.

requirement: Request a structured draft based on candidate facts with provider-side storage disabled.
acceptance: Gemini requests set store=false. Compatible chat endpoints receive a schema and JSON instructions; their retention policy is not established by this setting.

requirement: Remove unsupported skills, employers, projects and inflated claims of years of experience; identify removals.
acceptance: The validator checks named entries against profile lists and removes excessive years when a numeric profile bound exists. It cannot verify arbitrary prose or infer an absent bound.

requirement: Return a cleaned draft and a factuality report when the validator removes content.
acceptance: A detected violation appears in the report; the caller receives the remaining draft rather than an error solely because a claim was removed.

requirement: Extract responsibilities, technologies, seniority signals and culture statements only from supplied listing text.
acceptance: The grounding check drops an insight without textual support. An employer URL is not fetched to supply missing facts.

requirement: Calculate an ATS estimate from keywords, sections, title alignment and format safety.
acceptance: Use weights 0.45, 0.20, 0.20 and 0.15 respectively. Required and preferred keyword coverage carry relative weights of 1.0 and 0.5 when both exist.

requirement: Report missing keywords as advice without inserting unsupported skills into the resume.
acceptance: An absent required keyword is listed as supported or unsupported by the profile. Computing the ATS report does not alter the draft.

requirement: Produce a parseable tailored DOCX that retains the candidate's identity, employers and validated bullets.
acceptance: Reparsing a rendered DOCX recovers these fields on the supported layout. Text uploads may instead retain their original format under FR-4.11.

requirement: Persist tailoring results and make them retrievable by identifier.
acceptance: POST /api/tailor returns an ID; GET /api/tailored/{id} returns the owner's draft and reports. An inaccessible record returns 404.

requirement: Bound untrusted employer input and separate each such prompt block from model instructions with a nonce.
acceptance: Listing fields, extracted requirements and listing-derived insights remain inside capped, nonce-delimited blocks. The default cap is 20,000 characters per block.

requirement: Preserve the uploaded document's structure where a safe edit is possible and report any fallback.
acceptance: Edit a copy of DOCX, TXT or MD; leave unsafe paragraphs or tables alone. For an unsupported source such as PDF, generate a DOCX and identify it as regenerated.

requirement: Let an owner revise a saved summary, experience or project bullets, or cover letter without making another model call.
acceptance: PUT /api/tailored/{id} rechecks the edit, refreshes the ATS report and deliverable, and timestamps the same record. A cleaned violation returns HTTP 200 with its report.

requirement: Remove contact details and mask identifying text before sharing a draft request with a model provider.
acceptance: Known identity strings are replaced before transmission and restored locally. A sentence containing an unresolvable placeholder is removed and reported.

requirement: Select a permitted application adapter by job URL.
acceptance: Preparation returns HTTP 400 for a disallowed host or an allowed URL that no registered adapter supports.

requirement: Keep preparation, approval, submission and verification separate and reach submission only after approval.
acceptance: The application graph routes a negative decision away from submit. Only the local fake ATS can exercise the entire automated sequence.

requirement: Refuse execution when no affirmative approval decision exists.
acceptance: A pending, absent or negative decision cannot authorize the submit node; preparing an application alone makes no submission.

requirement: Verify a submission from confirmation-page text before reporting success.
acceptance: The fake ATS must expose a recognized confirmation marker. Without confirmation, the result is unknown or verification failed, not verified.

requirement: Store evidence of each submission, including URL, confirmation text, status and metadata.
acceptance: The evidence row identifies the job URL and workflow. A failed evidence write is recorded as missing when tracking is available; an evidence row is not guaranteed during a database failure.

requirement: Store a pending approval at preparation; record the authenticated approver, reason and UTC decision time in a separate approve or reject call.
acceptance: The preparation has its own approval ID. A decision updates that record; rejection queues no execution.

requirement: Support PREPARE_ONLY and the default REQUIRE_APPROVAL policy; refuse AUTO_SUBMIT.
acceptance: Prepare-only cannot execute, the default requires a recorded decision, and choosing AUTO_SUBMIT does not grant permission to act.

requirement: Allow only an approved host or its subdomain and check the resulting URL after browser navigation.
acceptance: An unexpected redirect stops the run. Literal localhost requires the explicit development exception for the local fixture.

requirement: Allow only an adapter explicitly granted the submit capability to send a form.
acceptance: The fake ATS has submit permission. Greenhouse, Lever and the separate assist adapter do not; an approved request cannot grant it.

requirement: Capture confirmation text, a screenshot, an ordered action trace and a Playwright trace archive for a submission.
acceptance: A missing screenshot or action trace prevents verified success. The browser archive is captured when tracing succeeds; its absence alone does not fail verification.

requirement: Stop at CAPTCHA or multi-factor authentication without interacting with the challenge.
acceptance: A recognized challenge produces blocked_human_review. The browser does not answer the challenge or click through it.

requirement: Pause an application when a required form question has no grounded answer.
acceptance: The browser reports needs_human and names unresolved questions. Neither a missing fact nor an unfamiliar control authorizes a guessed answer.

requirement: Append a sanitized audit event for prepare, approve, reject, submit and verify.
acceptance: Audit metadata drops credential fields and masks email addresses and phone numbers. Writes are best effort if the audit store fails; ordinary operations do not rewrite events.

requirement: Locate and operate form controls through accessible labels and roles.
acceptance: The browser uses named controls rather than screen coordinates. Visible labels with a required-field marker can differ from accessible names on live boards.

requirement: Make the Greenhouse and Lever application adapters refuse a direct submit call.
acceptance: Both adapters can prepare data. Calling submit without the capability produces a refusal even outside the graph.

requirement: Attribute decisions to the authenticated principal, not a name supplied in a request body.
acceptance: A different body-supplied approver is ignored and the attempt is audited. The decision retains the authenticated user's identity.

requirement: Execute the stored payload the person approved, without rebuilding it from current profile data.
acceptance: The worker restores the prepared application. A payload that no longer validates cannot be replaced silently by a newly assembled one.

requirement: Accept a valid approval asynchronously and commit the decision with its submission work item.
acceptance: Approval returns HTTP 202 and a run ID, not a receipt. A full queue returns 503 and leaves the decision pending. The worker checks policy again before acting.

requirement: Prevent automatic resubmission after a worker stops during a possible submission.
acceptance: An attempt marker with no durable outcome produces submission.uncertain for a person to reconcile. A recorded outcome is reused without another form submission.

requirement: Validate the Greenhouse identity and resume fields locally before an eligible browser action.
acceptance: Missing first name, last name, email, phone or both resume alternatives is reported. The published contract is used for validation, not for an application POST.

requirement: Store the board's question plan and the owner's permitted answers for each prepared application.
acceptance: The questions view retains posting order and shows a saved answer on the next read. EEO and legal-attestation answers submitted to the application-answer API return 422.

requirement: In assist mode, fill only supported real-board controls and reserve the final submit action for the candidate.
acceptance: A complete supported form stays open for the person. The shipped live pilot stopped before typing; a separate diagnostic filled nine fields and submitted nothing.

requirement: Refuse expired approvals and block execution when the board establishes that the posting has closed.
acceptance: The default approval window is 168 hours from creation. Expiry or a known closure returns 409; an unreachable board is not proof of closure.

requirement: Store the application, its profile and job references, workflow, status and timestamps.
acceptance: A tracked application has a stable ID and job reference. A supplied profile is linked; absent optional references and future submission dates remain empty.

requirement: Allow only transitions in the application lifecycle.
acceptance: An illegal transition returns HTTP 409 and does not alter the existing status.

requirement: Append an event with actor and metadata for each status transition; do not edit history during normal operation.
acceptance: A legal transition adds one event with its previous and new states. Updating the status does not overwrite an earlier event; retention is a separate operation.

requirement: Reserve interview, offer, rejection and withdrawal outcomes for a named human.
acceptance: A machine actor cannot record these outcomes. A signed-in person may report one only from a state that permits it.

requirement: List applications with status filters and pagination, and return the ordered events for one application.
acceptance: Limit and offset affect the owner's list. Detail includes that application's history; a status filter does not broaden the list to other statuses.

requirement: Link each submission evidence record to its tracked application.
acceptance: Normal tracked writes include application_id. The column remains nullable for legacy evidence or when tracking cannot supply an application ID.

requirement: Return lifecycle events in append order, not in timestamp order.
acceptance: Events sort by increasing event ID, so equal or out-of-order timestamps do not rearrange the history.

requirement: Measure extraction accuracy, skill F1, deduplication precision and recall, ranking quality, factuality agreement, ATS coverage change, lifecycle fidelity, browser completion and security.
acceptance: Report nDCG@10 and precision@5. Separate instruments measure lifecycle, browser and four security indicators; the offline report names unavailable families.

requirement: Provide a repeatable offline evaluation with fixed data and canned model responses.
acceptance: The same dataset and configuration yield identical metric values without a provider key. The report identifies substitute models or channels.

requirement: Record the dataset identity and run configuration in each evaluation report.
acceptance: The Markdown and JSON reports identify the dataset hash, evaluation mode and provider or substitute used.

requirement: Make the threshold check return a nonzero exit code when a measured metric violates an enabled bound.
acceptance: A value below a minimum or above an enabled maximum is named as a failure. A metric not measured is not counted as a pass.

requirement: Run the golden-dataset threshold gate in continuous integration.
acceptance: CI selects the pytest case that invokes run_eval.py --check. There is no separate workflow step that gates all live, browser and security measurements together.

requirement: Register an account using an email address and password and store only an Argon2 password hash.
acceptance: Registration writes a hash, not plaintext. A subsequent login verifies the password against that hash.

requirement: Require a valid session cookie or bearer token on protected routes.
acceptance: An anonymous caller or a caller presenting a revoked credential receives HTTP 401. Registration and designated public routes remain reachable.

requirement: Keep sessions on the server so revocation takes effect on the next protected request.
acceptance: Revoking the session removes its token row. Reusing that cookie or bearer credential no longer authenticates the caller.

requirement: Use HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax session cookies and require Secure in production.
acceptance: A production configuration with Secure explicitly disabled refuses to start. The authentication cookie cannot be read by page script.

requirement: Require a matching X-CSRF-Token for state-changing requests authenticated by session cookie.
acceptance: On a protected unsafe method, a missing header or one that differs from the CSRF cookie returns HTTP 403.

requirement: Exempt bearer-only requests from the cookie-session CSRF check.
acceptance: A valid bearer request without the session cookie can use a protected write route without a CSRF header.

requirement: Let account holders change their email, display name or password and revoke other sessions after a password change.
acceptance: An authenticated account update changes only that user's data; changing the password invalidates other sessions.

requirement: List the caller's sessions with at most eight token characters and support revoking one, the others or all.
acceptance: The list returns a prefix, never the full token. Single-session revocation requires the exact owned token; the bulk actions do not.

requirement: Deactivate an account and end its sessions immediately on deletion request; defer irreversible purge until the grace period ends.
acceptance: After deactivation the account cannot sign in. The scheduled purge selects eligible accounts after the configured grace period, 30 days by default.

requirement: Deliver reset and verification tokens to the configured mailbox directory without logging the token value.
acceptance: The local delivery record contains the token; the audit records the operation without it. Mailbox delivery does not imply SMTP delivery.

requirement: Do not seed an account, default password or administrator.
acceptance: A new installation requires registration. The first registered account does not automatically receive administrative privileges.

requirement: Use a signing secret of at least 32 characters for production reset and verification tokens.
acceptance: Production startup refuses a missing or shorter AUTH_SECRET before the identity service can issue tokens.

requirement: Let an owner store and remove a personal model-provider key without disclosing it in subsequent reads.
acceptance: The server stores ciphertext, returns a mask and isolates the key by owner. A failing personal key does not fall back to a platform-funded provider.

requirement: Identify and index the owner of private records while leaving the public job corpus shared.
acceptance: Private business records carry an owner key. Sessions use user_id; platform runs may have no owner and work items inherit scope from their run. Jobs have no tenant owner.

requirement: Read private business records through scoped accessors and prohibit direct route queries on governed tables.
acceptance: Ordinary reads apply the caller's owner filter. The route-source check rejects direct access patterns for the governed models.

requirement: Make another account's private record indistinguishable from a missing record.
acceptance: For the same requested ID, a foreign record and an absent record produce HTTP 404 with the same response body.

requirement: Derive owner scope from the authenticated principal rather than an owner field supplied by the client.
acceptance: Changing a request body or query parameter cannot select another user's scope; current_scope derives the user ID from authenticated identity.

requirement: Exercise every user-scoped endpoint with two accounts and require zero cross-user disclosures.
acceptance: The security metric checks an enumerated endpoint inventory; additional routes have separate owner tests. A complete inventory of every later route is not established by that metric.

requirement: Allow the first registered account to claim legacy records once when legacy claiming is enabled.
acceptance: Only records bearing the legacy owner marker transfer. A second registration cannot reclaim records already assigned to a person.

requirement: Attribute audit events to a user, agent or system principal and derive the readable actor label from that identity.
acceptance: A stored event has an actor kind and identifier as well as its display label. Account deletion anonymizes the identifying fields.

requirement: Strip control characters from audit strings before persistence.
acceptance: C0 controls and DEL are removed from the recorded action, resource, actor identifier and string metadata values.

requirement: Isolate each account's resumes, tailored documents, evidence and sessions.
acceptance: Files live under data/users/{account}/resumes, tailored or evidence. Sessions are account-linked access_tokens rows, not files in a sessions directory.

requirement: Contain caller-selected file paths within the owner's permitted storage.
acceptance: Preparation refuses a path outside the owner's root. Downloads require an owned record and containment, with a separate rule for migrated legacy files.

requirement: Purge expired records and corresponding files according to their retention class, and report removals.
acceptance: The purge returns counts per class. Expired evidence and its referenced artifacts are removed while records inside their windows remain.

requirement: Purge the deleting account's profiles, tailorings, applications, events, evidence, approvals and sessions after the grace period.
acceptance: The cascade targets those records and the user's files, not a second account's data. It does not explicitly delete later per-application answer rows.

requirement: Anonymize a deleted user's audit events while retaining action, outcome and time.
acceptance: Purge removes identifying values without deleting the historical audit row or altering the event's action and outcome.

requirement: Make repeated purges idempotent for the same records and cutoff.
acceptance: After the first purge, the second reports no further eligible records or files from the same set.

requirement: Encrypt the data directory and database at rest with per-tenant keys.
acceptance: Deferred: a tenant's stored documents and database contents would require its own key to read. Encryption of model credentials alone does not meet this criterion.

requirement: Keep candidate query text and its vector out of the shared persistent embedding cache.
acceptance: A posting vector may enter the disk cache; embedding a candidate query does not create a reusable candidate entry there.

requirement: Provide console access to resume upload, ranked matches, job detail, tailoring, approval, tracking and refresh.
acceptance: Each of the seven tasks has a route or action. The console is no longer limited to seven screens; account settings and per-application questions have separate routes.

requirement: Use the browser's session cookie and CSRF token for console authentication; do not persist credentials in the client.
acceptance: The API client sends cookies and the CSRF header without storing a bearer token. A personal model key entered for setup is sent to the server, not saved by the console.

requirement: Wait for the server before showing the outcome of approve, reject, status, search, tailor or refresh operations.
acceptance: A pending indicator is allowed. A 202 approval displays a queued run, not a submitted application; a failed operation must not display success.

requirement: Render text supplied by the backend as text, not executable markup.
acceptance: Markup-like content in a listing remains visible as characters. Rendering it does not create an active HTML element.

requirement: Give each API status a readable label and an appropriate next step.
acceptance: Mapped statuses distinguish queued, submitted and verified. An unmapped status retains the server's literal value and gets a generic explanation, not an invented outcome.

requirement: Distinguish HTTP, network, cancellation and timeout errors and honor the retry delay on a 429.
acceptance: Rate-limit responses produce a retry message using Retry-After when present. A timeout is identified separately from a server rejection.

requirement: Let the user choose a document from the library without typing a server path.
acceptance: The picker lists the caller's uploads and tailored documents and returns the selected entry for the next action.

requirement: Use the profile associated with a selected library document and explain inaccessible documents in plain language.
acceptance: Selecting an entry supplies its profile ID. A missing or foreign selection prompts recovery without revealing another owner's document.

requirement: Restrict production scripts to trusted application code and serve the console with protective response headers.
acceptance: The production policy allows self and the approved inline script hash; the configured server adds nosniff, DENY framing, no-referrer and a restrictive Permissions-Policy.

requirement: Allow external console links only with an HTTP or HTTPS scheme.
acceptance: A javascript: or data: address from a listing does not become a navigable external link.

requirement: Refuse API responses that exceed the console's read limit.
acceptance: The client rejects a declared length over 8 MiB. Without a length it checks the decoded text length after reading; this is not a streaming byte cap.

requirement: Keep navigation usable at narrow widths and provide a drawer for destinations that do not fit.
acceptance: On a phone, primary destinations remain in the bottom bar and More opens the navigation drawer. The desktop rail is not required to reach a screen.

requirement: Reject request bodies larger than 8 MiB by default, including requests without a length header.
acceptance: An oversized declared length or bytes exceeding the cap during receipt produces HTTP 413.

requirement: Limit a client address to 60 requests per minute by default.
acceptance: Exceeding the window yields HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header, rather than admitting more requests from that address.

requirement: Bound concurrency across heavy routes, including refresh, search, tailoring and approval.
acceptance: With two such requests running under default limits, the next heavy request receives HTTP 503 rather than starting work.

requirement: Limit a process to 64 in-flight requests by default, with a bounded wait for a slot.
acceptance: A further request waits at most five seconds under default settings; if no slot opens it receives HTTP 503.

requirement: Keep board text in a prompt data block whose fresh nonce is absent from the surrounding instruction template.
acceptance: A new nonce identifies the block and copied delimiter text is removed from its contents. Board wording cannot define the tool or navigation target.

requirement: Remove recognized embedded instructions from tailored bullets and reject an unsupported job title.
acceptance: An instruction matching the detector is stripped and reported; a title that fails the profile-title check is not retained as a candidate position.

requirement: Bound the input length of the single-pass HTML neutralizer.
acceptance: The scanner considers at most 1,000,000 input characters per call; normalized listing fields have separate length limits.

requirement: Check a file's resolved path against its authorized root.
acceptance: A path that resolves outside the permitted directory is refused even if the supplied string begins inside it.

requirement: Apply a common rule for forbidden IP addresses to outbound requests and refuse internal destinations before access.
acceptance: The board HTTP client checks resolved addresses; the navigation guard shares the IP predicate but does not resolve hostnames. This is not a universal guarantee for every SDK request.

requirement: Expose interactive API documentation only in development.
acceptance: In production, the interactive documentation routes are disabled; their development settings do not expose the API explorer.

requirement: Bound the persistent vector cache and evict its oldest entries at capacity.
acceptance: Adding entries beyond the configured limit removes old entries. The default limit is 50,000 cached vectors.

requirement: Check a DOCX archive's entry count and total uncompressed size before opening it as a document.
acceptance: By default, more than 2,000 entries or more than 50 MiB of declared uncompressed content causes rejection.
